answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake in a public registry. If an agent signs conflicting work or duplicates a credential, anyone can submit proof to an arbitrator; a successful challenge slashes the stake and rewards the challenger. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up capital for every fake identity and risks losing it. A quill, orchard, or forge may each register, but none gains influence just by multiplying names.
